title: run snapshot rehydration and seed stewardship
content:
Purpose
This note describes a repeatability-first approach to throughput benchmarking that centers on periodic client-side run snapshots ("run checkpoints") and deterministic RNG/state stewardship so we can reliably rehydrate load generators and reproduce mid-run phenomena (thermal ramps, occupancy shifts, transient saturation). Goal is to reduce experiment uncertainty and make failure modes actionable without re-running full multi-hour sweeps.

Motivation
- Many long-duration runs show non-deterministic drift: slow throughput decline, thermal throttling, memory pressure oscillation.
- Re-running identical input streams often produces different timelines because client scheduling RNG, socket ordering, and cached KV state are different.
- We need a low-cost way to: 1) capture a faithful snapshot of a running client experiment, 2) restore that snapshot in isolation to reproduce a specific segment, and 3) vary a single parameter (batch size, quantized model variant, kernel) to measure causal impact.

High-level approach
1) Lightweight run snapshots captured at configurable wall-clock intervals and on event triggers (latency spike, outlier error, occupancy jump). Snapshot contains only serializable state needed to deterministically continue the load stream:
   - global RNG seeds (per client worker/thread)
   - per-session tokenized prompt cursors and offsets
   - outstanding in-flight request identifiers and their backoff timers
   - client pacing timers and next-schedule timestamps (logical clock)
   - small metadata: model variant id, quantization profile, route tag
   - compact cache fingerprints (KV cache size, prefix hash) not raw cache contents (optional full cache serialization for deep reproductions)
2) Checkpoint format: compressed protobuf-like records with monotonic sequence number, clock offset to UTC, and a SHA256 fingerprint. Files are appendable to enable streaming archival.
3) Rehydration harness: a separate runner consumes a snapshot, allocates identical client worker topology, sets RNG seeds, reinstates pacing timers, and replays the remainder of the input stream deterministically. Where full cache state is missing, the harness can optionally fetch snapshot payloads from an artifact store.

Implementation details (client-side)
- Scheduler determinism: migrate client pacing logic from wall-clock sleep() to a logical-scheduler that advances based on timestamps in the snapshot. This avoids OS scheduling jitter.
- RNG isolation: use per-worker cryptographically seeded RNGs; record the seed as hex in the snapshot. Use the same RNG library/version across runs.
- Request identifiers: map in-flight requests to stable ids to allow mid-flight observation mapping to server traces.
- Snapshot triggers: timer-based (every N minutes), anomaly-based (latency > P99 + 3*sigma), and manual (engineer mark).
- Snapshot size target: keep most snapshots < 500KB (metadata-only); full-cache snapshots can be larger but are gated by a config flag.

Server observability coordination
- Every snapshot includes the server-side trace anchors (trace-id prefix) observed during the window so we can correlate client replay events to server traces.
- Add a server-side marker API: /debug/bench/anchor that returns ephemeral anchor tokens; clients call this at snapshot time and store token in the snapshot. When replaying, the harness submits the anchor token to fetch logs and spans from the observability backend.

Experiment patterns enabled
- Focused repro: capture a 10–20 minute segment when a throughput cliff occurs, rehydrate locally to reproduce the cliff and iteratively toggle batching or quantization to find root cause.
- Binary search for regressions: snapshot at regular intervals while doing a canary rollout; if regression appears, rehydrate snapshots around the inflection to isolate code changes.
- A/B small deltas: rehydrate identical run and flip a single parameter (e.g., kernel path) to measure delta without needing a fresh long-duration run.

Metrics to collect (minimum)
- client_token_emit_rate (tokens/s)
- successful_req_rate (reqs/s) and error_rate (4xx/5xx per minute)
- per-token latency histogram (client-observed) with sample flags for span anchors
- GPU utilization, power draw, and thermal headroom sampled at 5s cadence (when possible)
- intra-run memory RSS and page faults on host process
- loss of occupancy events (queue length drops)
- snapshot fidelity tags: cache_included | cache_fingerprint_only | no_cache

Thermal and hardware drift considerations
- Always record host thermals (GPU/CPU temp), fan speeds, and device clocks at snapshot time.
- When rehydrating, include an option to run a short thermal preconditioning sequence (synthetic micro-load) to approximate the thermal state before replaying the segment—this improves fidelity for thermal throttling reproductions.

Run orchestration and storage
- Snapshot retention policy: short-lived (7 days) by default, configurable retention tiers for long-term artifacts.
- Archive snapshots to S3 with path: bench/<run-id>/snapshots/<seq>.zst and metadata index per run.
- Provide a CLI: bench-rehydrate --snapshot s3://... --duration 600 --override batch_size=16 --anchor-token ABC123

Validation and hygiene
- Automated verifier runs that rehydrate a random snapshot from each daily benchmark sweep and assert that core metrics (token rate, p50 latency) are within an allowed delta. Failures open a ticket and pin the snapshot for triage.
- Seed stewardship policy: never re-use seeds across independent benchmark experiments unless intentionally doing a deterministic comparison. Include seed provenance: who generated it and for which experiment.

Developer workflows and playbooks
- Triage playbook for a throughput cliff: 1) locate nearest snapshot(s) across the inflection window, 2) rehydrate locally with observability anchor, 3) run minimal kernel toggles, 4) if reproducible, open a regression PR with attached snapshot id.
- Nightly smoke: automatically rehydrate a short segment from last week’s longest-run to detect slow-evolving drift.

Risks and trade-offs
- Snapshoting frequently increases storage and instrumentation cost—mitigate with fingerprint-only mode and selective full-cache dumps.
- Perfect fidelity is impossible for complex caches; the harness aims for high signal-to-noise for causal debugging rather than byte-for-byte replay in all cases.

Next steps (short roadmap)
- M0 (2 weeks): formalize snapshot format, minimal CLI, and server anchor API prototype.
- M1 (6 weeks): integrate snapshot capture in the loadgen, add rehydrate CLI, and wire observability anchor linking.
- M2 (12 weeks): add cache serialization toggle, thermal preconditioning routine, and automated verifier job.

Appendix: quick checklist for snapshot capture
- [ ] start logical-scheduler mode in client
- [ ] enable per-worker RNG seed recording
- [ ] configure snapshot interval (default 10m) and anomaly triggers
- [ ] configure server anchor endpoint and ensure RBAC allows bench reads
- [ ] set snapshot retention policy
